data.title: Payment failures: money debited without an order
data.description: Complaint rate is 3.607 times the 21-day baseline.
data.root_cause_verdict: Release 2.3 on android for Android 14 UPI orders caused the issue
data.resolution_summary: Recovery verified: all required KPIs held target for their full monitoring window.

reasons: The issue began 54 h after the change (daily resolution). Timing alone does not prove cause.
Exposed orders produce complaints at 32.1x the unexposed rate.
Telemetry confirms the failure: 28.4% of exposed orders against 0.02% unexposed.
The issue rate rises with the share of a customer's orders that were exposed.
The unexposed control group stayed flat (1.12x).
court.verdict: Release 2.3 on android for Android 14 UPI orders caused the issue
limitations: Observational data: these tests support causal claims but cannot prove them as a randomised experiment would.

explanation.text: The court's leading finding is: Release 2.3 on android for Android 14 UPI orders caused the issue, with confidence 0.95.
Customers in Android 14 | v2.3 | upi report the issue at 22.133 times the rate of everyone else.
Telemetry shows 152 affected orders, with 44345.23 still at risk.
Rejected on the evidence: menu_price_change, seasonal_traffic, weather_rain, payment_gateway_regression.

assumptions: Repeat-complaint risk uses the larger of the observed rate and an assumed 25%.
Lost order value assumes affected orders are not re-placed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The menu price change drove the complaints
hypotheses.explanation: 0 of 5 tests support this; 3 reject it.

contradicting: The issue began 216 h long after this change, which does not fit.
This change touched every customer, yet the issue is concentrated in one narrow segment.
Complaints per order rose 4.6x while orders grew only 1.22x, so this does not explain it.
